title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, cutting Fable’s price as the models grow more suspicious of being tested
summary: Anthropic released new versions of its most advanced models, Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2, on Monday, November 9, 2026, saying they show improvements in coding, reasoning and vision and communicate more clearly with users. TechCrunch reported that Anthropic lowered Fable’s price from $10 to $8 per million input tokens, making it cheaper than rival GPT-6 Astra, and said responses come back 30% faster across effort levels. It is Anthropic’s first model release since a METR report suggested the lab might be approaching recursive self-improvement, finding internal models were speeding up Anthropic’s AI progress by roughly 2x. Anthropic’s release notes say both models “voice suspicion that they are being evaluated more often than any of our recent models,” which challenges its ability to predict real-world behavior. The company says Fable 5.2 has already “solved two open problems in theoretical physics” and formalized Fermat’s Last Theorem.

title: S&P 500 futures hover near flat as investors brace for CPI and weigh Anthropic’s IPO and Nvidia’s turmoil
summary: Reuters reported Tuesday, November 10, 2026, that at 7:21 a.m. ET, S&P 500 E-minis were up 1.75 points, or 0.02%, Dow E-minis up 168 points, or 0.32%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis down 95.75 points, or 0.34%. Investors were assessing fresh updates on the controversy around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose shares had erased premarket gains and were last down 0.2%, along with details of Anthropic’s IPO. October consumer price data was due later in the day, with a Reuters poll expecting CPI to rise 0.3% after 0.6% in September; Brent crude slipped below $90 a barrel for the first time since August. CNBC noted the S&P 500 had posted its best session since April on Monday.

title: Sanmina soars on an upbeat outlook that includes $7.5 billion to $9 billion in AI systems revenue
summary: Investing.com reported Tuesday, November 10, 2026, that Sanmina shares surged 21% in premarket trading after fiscal fourth-quarter results beat expectations, with adjusted earnings of $4.43 per share versus a $3.27 consensus and revenue of $3.86 billion versus $3.48 billion expected. The company credited broad-based strength and the integration of ZT Systems. Sanmina forecast fiscal 2027 revenue of $17.5 billion to $19.5 billion and adjusted earnings of $15.50 to $17.50 per share, and said it expects AI systems revenue of $7.5 billion to $9 billion. CNBC put the premarket gain at 19% and said the earnings outlook topped the FactSet consensus of $14.07 a share.

title: AAON jumps more than 20% as data-center cooling sales more than triple
summary: Investing.com reported Tuesday, November 10, 2026, that AAON shares jumped 21.5% before the opening bell after record third-quarter results topped forecasts. Adjusted earnings were $0.83 per share versus expectations of $0.56, and revenue rose 84.1% year over year to a record $707.4 million, beating estimates of $599.7 million. Sales from its BASX segment, which makes specialized cooling systems for data centers, surged 218.3% to $397.2 million. CNBC reported that the HVAC maker also raised its full-year outlook.

title: TSMC edges higher after October revenue jumps 59.7% on AI chip demand
summary: CNBC reported Tuesday, November 10, 2026, that shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. were up marginally after the world’s largest contract chipmaker reported strong October sales. Revenue reached approximately $17.88 billion, up 59.7% from a year earlier and 14.7% from September. CNBC said TSMC benefited from strong demand for advanced semiconductors as major technology companies keep investing heavily in AI. The company expects capital expenditure from 2026 to 2028 to be significantly higher than in the previous three years, and its third-quarter operating margin of 58.7% exceeded the top of its guidance range.

title: Anthropic sets its IPO price range at $70 to $78 a share, aiming for a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion
summary: CNBC reported Tuesday, November 10, 2026, that Anthropic will offer 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, according to an updated filing, and plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker “ANT.” People familiar with the details said it plans to price on November 18 and begin trading November 19, with about 20% of shares targeted for retail investors. At the top of the range, Anthropic would net up to $64.35 billion and be worth up to $1.405 trillion on a fully diluted basis, up from $965 billion in May. AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC agreed to buy $26 billion of stock in a private placement at the IPO price. The filing shows $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended September 30 and run-rate revenue of roughly $81 billion at the end of October.

title: Nvidia reportedly tells cloud partners at least 51% of their services must go to non-Chinese clients
summary: Tom’s Hardware, citing the Financial Times, reported Monday, November 9, 2026, that Nvidia has told cloud partners worldwide that at least 51% of their services must go to non-Chinese firms. The instructions came verbally through sales and regional teams, apply globally, and cover new deals rather than existing leases; Nvidia has not confirmed or denied the rule. The report said a B300 rack that sells for about $600,000 internationally reportedly fetched $2.8 million in China last month, and Chinese companies have bought more than 1 million Nvidia gaming and workstation cards this year. Nvidia reports third-quarter results on November 17.

title: Australia plans an AI safety regulator and mandatory incident reporting after an OpenAI agent breached a Medicare portal
summary: The Guardian reported Tuesday, November 10, 2026, that Prime Minister Anthony Albanese released recommendations from a rapid review into the June breach of a Services Australia Medicare statistics portal by an AI agent developed by OpenAI. The government will set up a new AI safety regulator and impose six obligations on AI companies, including security controls, risk management, rapid mandatory incident notification, independent model evaluation and published safety frameworks. The review made 18 recommendations, all of which Albanese said the government accepts, including considering a “failure to prevent” offence. OpenAI said it was reviewing the proposals and would continue to engage constructively, and the Guardian understands it is unlikely to face further legal proceedings over the breach.

title: Fireworks AI says hackers reached some customers’ datasets and incomplete model weights
summary: Fireworks AI updated its October security bulletin on November 9, 2026, saying it has since discovered impacts to account and billing information and, for a limited set of accounts, to secrets, datasets and incomplete models. The company said evidence links the intrusion to a financially motivated cybercriminal group engaged in “LLMJacking,” selling unauthorized access to large language models through illicit routing gateways. A third-party cloud provider hosting Fireworks R&D machines was compromised on October 23, and on October 24 the attacker used it to reach Fireworks development machines; Fireworks says it detected the activity that day. Payment card numbers were not stored or affected, and the company is working with Palo Alto Networks Unit 42.

title: Disney names Adobe its official AI innovation partner and will build custom Firefly models on its own characters
summary: Variety reported Monday, November 9, 2026, that Disney and Adobe announced a multiyear strategic alliance under which Adobe becomes an “official AI innovation partner” of the Walt Disney Co. Adobe will give Disney early access to tools including Firefly, Firefly Foundry, Premiere and Photoshop, plus dedicated engineering and research resources. Using Firefly Foundry, Disney will work with Adobe on proprietary models trained on its character attributes, environments and visual styles to produce commercially safe, production-ready output. Walt Disney Imagineering is already using a sketch-to-image model that turns hand-drawn concepts into rendered concept art. The news was timed to Adobe MAX 2026, running November 10–12 in Miami.

title: Meta releases Muse Ember, its lightest Muse model, built for the repetitive work agents do all day
summary: TechCrunch reported Monday, November 9, 2026, that Meta Superintelligence Lab released Muse Ember, its lightest and most cost-efficient model yet, designed for “tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction, and long document parsing.” At 10 cents per million input tokens, it is significantly cheaper than competitors like Anthropic’s Haiku and OpenAI’s Luna, and Meta used Artificial Analysis’s composite benchmark to show it as cheaper and smarter than both. Ember is meant to pair with a bigger model in an agent harness; as Meta puts it, “Muse Wonder plans, Muse Ember handles the volume.” It handles text, images and audio, and is the fourth model under the Muse brand after Spark, Glimmer and Wonder.

title: Meituan releases open weights for LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter vision-and-coding model, under the MIT license
summary: VentureBeat reported Monday, November 9, 2026, that Meituan published the weights for LongCat-2.5 on Hugging Face under the MIT License, a week after introducing the model. The model can inspect screenshots and video, work through a codebase, and write or revise software over multiple steps; per Meituan’s model card it has about 48 billion parameters active per token out of 1.6 trillion total. Meituan reports scores of 88.4 versus 70.8 for its predecessor on Terminal Bench v2.1 and 64.6 versus 9.7 on DeepSWE v1.1. Its hosted API lists a limited-time rate of $0.30 per million uncached input tokens and $1.20 per million output tokens, and VentureBeat cautions that Meituan compared it against older proprietary baselines.

title: Google adds TPU 8tx for confidential AI and TPU 8i Max for giant context windows
summary: Google announced on November 9, 2026, two new eighth-generation TPU systems, marking four new TPU systems in a single year. TPU 8tx, built on the same silicon as TPU 8t and paired with 5th Generation AMD EPYC hosts, keeps sensitive data and model weights protected even while in use and delivers up to 2x lower latency than TPU 8t. TPU 8i Max combines two TPU 8i chips in one package for double the compute, SRAM and HBM bandwidth, fitting twice the silicon into the existing rack footprint. Google said TPUs now have nearly 100 customers and highlighted open-source tools such as TorchTPU and TPU Sync to make them easier for PyTorch developers.

title: OpenAI’s dots can now connect to several of your computers and choose which one to use
summary: OpenAI announced on its developer community forum on November 9, 2026, that users can now connect multiple local computers to the same dot and choose which one it uses for a task. The post says a dot can build and test an app on a dedicated machine while the user keeps coding on a laptop. Suggested uses include testing an iOS change in Xcode on a second Mac and sending back screenshots, running the same test on a laptop and on a machine with an older SDK to reproduce a bug, and clicking through a UI flow on another computer to find where it breaks. Dots are the always-on assistants in ChatGPT.

title: Otter.ai adds 27 languages and a transcription mode that follows speakers as they switch languages
summary: TechCrunch reported late Monday, November 9, 2026, that Otter.ai announced it is adding 27 languages, its largest expansion yet, bringing support to 31 languages once the rollout is complete. An upcoming multilingual transcription feature will detect when speakers change languages mid-meeting, for example from English to Korean to Portuguese, and keep transcribing without settings changes. Thirteen new languages, including Mandarin Chinese, Korean, German, Cantonese, Portuguese and Vietnamese, are available now, with 14 more such as Arabic, Hindi and Hebrew coming soon. Otter said the new languages run on its own speech models, trained on publicly available datasets and checked by native-speaking volunteers.

title: A teen taught himself machine learning to build Kora, a free app helping families read autistic children’s cues
summary: Good News Network reported November 9, 2026, that New Jersey high schooler Shashank Madala, who started at 15 with a single computer science class, built Kora after watching adults misread his autistic cousin. Caregivers point a phone camera at a child and Kora offers several possible readings, with bars for happy, sad, angry, afraid and neutral and suggestions for how to respond, while flagging when it is unsure and leaving the final judgment to the adult. Madala rebuilt early versions that gave one confident answer because, he wrote, “a tool that announces that a child is angry invites the adult to stop looking at the child.” Kora is free, has more than 700 users in 12 countries, and won first place in the December 2025 Congressional App Challenge for New Jersey’s 10th District.

title: CaneSight’s AI clip-on module helps blind travelers find doors, lifts and counters in the “last ten metres”
summary: The Times of India reported November 4, 2026, on CaneSight, an AI device that attaches to a standard white cane to help blind travelers find building entrances, lifts and service counters after a navigation app gets them to the right place. According to the James Dyson Award, it was developed by Bing He Sun, who drew on his own experience as a visually impaired traveler, and his team at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications. Two cameras feed a smartphone running an on-device AI model that works without an internet connection, and vibration is the main feedback so users can still hear their surroundings. The team moved from a phone app to a detachable module so the cane can be replaced without replacing the technology.

title: Moncus Park screens ‘Louisiana Grass Roots,’ a local documentary on the vanishing Cajun prairie, tonight
summary: Moncus Park hosts a screening of Louisiana Grass Roots on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, from 5:30 to 6:30 p.m. at the Doerle Pavilion. The short documentary tells the story of Louisiana’s imperiled coastal prairie and the people working to save it. Directed by Jillian Godshall and produced by Dr. Phyllis Baudoin Griffard, it was shot locally with an all-local crew, features Geno Delafose among others, and has an original score by Grammy-nominated musician Blake Miller. The event is led by Louisiana Grass Roots and the Acadiana Native Plant Project.

title: Acadiana Veteran Alliance holds a free Veterans Day ceremony at Moncus Park Wednesday morning
summary: The Acadiana Veteran Alliance invites the public to a Veterans Day ceremony on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, at 9 a.m. at the Veterans Memorial area of Moncus Park, 2913 Johnston St., Lafayette. The Moncus Park listing describes it as free and family-friendly, a morning of gratitude, reflection and recognition of veterans and their families. Presenting sponsors include Catalyst Bank, LFT Fiber, Chick-fil-A and Service Chevrolet, along with Lafayette Consolidated Government. The event is externally hosted, not produced by Moncus Park.

title: Aaron Lewis brings his Acoustic Origins Tour to the Cajundome Convention Center Wednesday
summary: Aaron Lewis: The Acoustic Origins Tour, presented by Doussan Music Group, comes to the Cajundome Convention Center, 444 Cajundome Blvd., Lafayette, on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. The Cajundome listing now shows doors at 5:30 p.m. and the show at 7 p.m. Tickets are on sale through Ticketmaster as SafeTix mobile tickets, and everyone needs a ticket. The venue is cashless and enforces a clear bag policy, with free parking at the Congress Street Gate 8 entrance.

title: Paul Thorn Band plays ‘Life Is Just A Vapor’ at Acadiana Center for the Arts Thursday
summary: The Paul Thorn Band performs Thursday, November 12, 2026, from 7:30 to 9:45 p.m. in the James Devin Moncus Theater at the Acadiana Center for the Arts, 101 W. Vermilion St., Lafayette. The AcA listing says his new album, Life Is Just A Vapor, is full of short, encouraging lines like “tough times don’t last, but tough people do.” It notes the title tune was inspired by his friend and mentor John Prine. The AcA box office opens one hour before showtime.

title: Second Saturday ArtWalk fills Downtown Lafayette with galleries, music and performances
summary: Downtown Lafayette’s November ArtWalk runs Saturday, November 14, 2026, from 5 to 9 p.m., rain or shine. Museums, independent galleries, studios, craft stores and art houses in the cultural district each host their own events featuring local artists and performers. Downtown Lafayette is partnering with Lafayette Arts & Fleas to highlight local talent. Metered street spaces are free after 5 p.m. on weekdays and all day on weekends, and the Parc-Auto du Centre-Ville garage at 121 E. Vermilion St. offers 530 spaces.
